acceptance_criteria.condition: Retrying one checkout request creates exactly one payment-gateway charge.

invariants: One checkout request must map to at most one charge.

safeguards.name: idempotency
safeguards.rationale: The payment gateway deduplicates requests using a stable key derived from the checkout request ID.

verification.result: The buggy path produced two gateway records; the stable-key intervention produced one.

remaining_risks: Production systems still require durable, transactionally stored idempotency keys across process restarts.

causal.symptom: A retried checkout request creates two payment charges.

evidence_artifacts.summary: Runs the duplicate-charge reproduction and stable-key intervention assertions.
Deterministic report emitted only after the reproduction and intervention tests pass.

hypotheses.claim: The UI displays a single charge twice.
hypotheses.prediction: The payment gateway contains one charge for the order.

hypotheses.claim: The checkout retry path changes the idempotency key for each attempt.
hypotheses.prediction: Using one stable key for both attempts produces one gateway charge.

causal.discriminating_check: Inspect gateway records, then retry with only the idempotency-key derivation changed.
causal.timeline_evidence: The first attempt and retry use the same request ID; only the retry attempt number changes before the second buggy charge is created.
